summary:
Wrote `plan.md`: all four modules share one column section. Fluted quartz-pillar Doric columns, spaced 8 apart, stand 4 blocks in front of a recessed diorite wall of tall windows, over a rusticated base, with a triglyph entablature, attic and balustrade. The portico and corner pavilion stand 1 block forward, and wing bays tile with no visible seam.
The portico carries six columns plus flanking pairs, three arched doorways reached by slab steps, and a pediment with relief.
Plot 0 sets a 46-across drum (16 paired columns, 8 tall windows, stepped attic) on the square pavilion. On it goes a lead-grey tuff dome with 16 andesite ribs and a gold band, then a columned lantern and gold cupola and finial to y 125. Gold appears only there, so the gilded dome over the colonnade is what makes it read as City Hall. Nothing was built or rendered, so none of this has been checked yet. A Beaux-Arts palace in four modules sharing one wing section: a rusticated diorite base, giant 2x2 quartz_pillar Doric columns standing 4 in front of a recessed wall of tall grey-glass windows, a triglyph entablature, an attic and a diorite balustrade, the pattern tiling seamlessly on a 4-block grid.
The portico adds three arched doorways with slab steps, six columns plus flanking pairs and a calcite pediment carrying quartz relief. The corner pavilion turns the corner on pilastered antas under a taller panelled attic.
Plot 0 stacks the same order on four faces, a drum ringed by 16 paired columns, a 2-thick polished_tuff dome (16 andesite ribs, gold band, ring and cartouches, glowstone in the inner shell), and a columned gold-cupola lantern to y 125. The design is written but not yet built or rendered.

rooms.name: Rotunda
rooms.purpose: The great domed hall of the monument, solemn grey and white, looking straight up through the drum into the glowing dome. No furniture. Floor medallion under the axis (andesite ring r9-10, calcite ring r4-5, chiseled quartz 2x2 centre) and 8 lamp standards on the r14 circle at the 45° axes; centre kept clear.
rooms.ways_in: No door inside the kit: entered from the wings when placed on the site. Base storey reaches x/z 5..58 at y 2..8; open above through the deck hole r18.5 at y 36 into the drum and dome.

rooms.name: Portico vestibule
rooms.purpose: The entrance hall behind the three arched doors: low, bright, cool stone. No furniture. Calcite/andesite paving bands leading in from each door to z 12, and hanging lanterns on a 6-grid under the y 9 floor; nothing in front of the doors.

recruit.why: Coursed rusticated granite with channel joints, recessed walls with lintels and spandrels, round drum walls, leaving every opening empty by not placing
Giant 2x2 fluted Doric shafts with foot and capital set on an exact 8-block rhythm and on the drum's angled pairs
Triglyph frieze, upside-down-stair cornices with corner pieces, balustrades, keystones, pediment relief figures and acroteria
A smooth hollow hemisphere with stair edges and 16 fine paler ribs that read as lead from the street
Gold only where City Hall has it: the dome's band, ring and cartouches, the lantern capitals, cupola and finial
Pane runs with correct connection states including the cross-module joint columns; bronze-dark door pairs with mirrored hinges and transoms
Mob-proofing a huge monument with lanterns hidden behind balustrades and loggias, chains in tall halls, and glowstone in the dome
